panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Coronal CT reconstruction in a human patient demonstrating left giant hydronephrosis with cortical thinning and dilated distal ureter just proximal to the ureterovesical junction, directly supporting primary obstructive megaureter as stated in the caption. panels.rationale: Single H&E micrograph of the human ureteral wall from a case of primary obstructive megaureter, with in-image annotation lines labelled A, B and C pointing to fibrotic stroma, chronic inflammatory infiltrate and hypertrophic smooth-muscle layer respectively. The caption explicitly documents hypertrophy of the muscular layer of the ureteral wall, which matches the vocabulary finding for primary obstructive megaureter histology; the accompanying article title and in-text statement attribute the specimen to primary obstructive megaureter. Fibrosis and chronic inflammation are clearly visible/described but absent from the vocabulary, so they are listed as proposed findings. The A/B/C labels are regions of one micrograph rather than separate panels, so the figure is treated as a single panel; no skin, ethnicity or age data are available.

in_text_mentions: colicky in nature, and radiated from the loin to the groin. He had no other specific complaints. On abdominal examination, there was tenderness over the left lumbar region and left iliac fossa, without signs of guarding or rigidity. Renal angle tenderness was also present. Renal function tests were within normal limits. A CT urogram revealed mild left hydroureteronephrosis and moderate-to-gross hydroureter, likely reflux-induced. Additional findings included a left ureteric calculus and a simple renal cyst on the left side, with normal morphology of the proximal ureter (Figure 1 and Figure 2).
